limitations: Cross-process target is created and owned by the test driver; no user application was injected.
Positive controls deliberately activate owned fixture windows, then restore the preceding foreground before guarded measurement. They are not counted as background success.
Foreground/pointer assertions sample boundaries; no claim of exhaustive continuous event monitoring.
A retained DLL reference remains until the disposable target exits, preventing unloading code still referenced by a subclass. Production unload is not implemented.
One target root and one UI thread per target process; new windows, new processes, multiple UI threads and real WeChat are not covered.
Initial WinForms raw mouse test did not deliver a button click. Its PerformClick check only verifies the activation primitive; actual input evidence comes from native and Qt cross-process cases.
A Qt harness foreground-restoration timing failure was corrected by bounded observation of the asynchronous transition before sending guarded input.
No formal MCP integration or release package.
